summary: Assist: incremental degrade script + tenant snapshot restore after optimizer profile caused latency/cost instability
description:
Issue summary:
Customer experienced a sudden increase in 95p/99p latency and per-request token cost after enabling a combined optimizer profile (aggressive async batching + KV-prefetch + mixed-precision quantization) for the redwood-open-4o-q2 model on dedicated capacity. Impact began ~2026-03-11 22:00 UTC and persisted with intermittent spikes.

Impact:
- BlueCrest production traffic saw 99p latency jump from ~220ms to 1.8s for session-based chat routes.
- Customer reports SLA alerts and a near-term cost surge (estimated +38% token/GPU cost).
- Several in-flight long sessions experienced partial streaming disconnects.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: dc-west-1 (reserved GPUs: 8x A100 per tenant cluster)
- Serving runtime: v2.14.0-optflags
- Recent config change: optimizer profile id opt-20260311-A (applied 2026-03-11 21:45 UTC)

Ask:
- Provide a safe, stepwise degrade script and assistance to restore a tenant snapshot if needed.
- Minimize request disruption and avoid wholesale tenant drain if possible.

Attached/linked telemetry: dashboard links included in comments.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) On a dedicated tenant, apply optimizer profile that enables: async batching aggressive, KV-prefetch enable, mixed-precision quantization (profile opt-20260311-A).
2) Route production traffic (session-based chat) and observe 95p/99p latency and streaming errors over 15-30m window.
3) Monitor GPU memory pressure and KV cache eviction metrics during steady-state and spike periods.
logs: 2026-03-11T22:03:12Z WARN serving-runtime: async-batch queue depth spike 18->72 for route /v1/chat/generate
2026-03-11T22:05:01Z ERROR streaming: client disconnect mid-stream (code=EPIPE) 3 instances
2026-03-11T22:07:44Z INFO scheduler: forced-evict kv-cache tenant=bluecrest ratio=0.62
investigation_notes:
Initial triage by Support: correlated change window with opt-20260311-A rollout. Observed patterns: higher async batching concurrency led to unpredictable queueing for mixed-length sessions; KV-prefetch introduced cache thrash on long-session workloads causing eviction storms; quantization introduced slightly higher decode CPU in fallback paths when GPU paths saturated. Memory pressure and eviction metrics line up with latency spikes. Hypothesis: interaction between aggressive async batch sizing + KV-prefetch warmed too many prefixes leading to eviction and backpressure, magnified by quantized kernels causing occasional slower token throughput.

Telemetry highlights:
- 95p latency: baseline 220ms -> spike 1.8s after change
- KV eviction rate: 0.04/sec -> 0.63/sec during spikes
- GPU utilization: 58% -> 96% transient spikes
- Token cost per request estimated +38% during peak window

Preliminary safe mitigations tested in staging: incremental reduce async-batch max-concurrency -> immediate reduction in 95p latency; disabling KV-prefetch eliminated eviction storms but increased average cost; rolling back quant profile reduced decode variance.
comments: 2026-03-12 09:12 - Aisha Patel (Customer): Noticed latency & cost alerts immediately after we applied the optimizer profile. Can Support help avoid truncating long sessions? We need minimal disruption — can't fully drain traffic.

2026-03-12 10:05 - Ethan Kim (Support): Thanks Aisha. We're triaging. Initial look suggests an interaction between async batching and KV-prefetch. Requesting permission to run a staged degrade on 5% traffic and capture telemetry for 20 minutes before wider rollout.

2026-03-12 11:30 - BlueCrest SRE (Customer): Approved 5% test. Dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood/tenants/bluecrest/opt-20260311-A - see spike windows. Note: long session route is /chat/session-stream.

2026-03-12 12:20 - Ethan Kim (Support): Deployed staged degrade script to 5% via traffic-split. Steps performed: reduced async-batch max_concurrency: 64->24, KV-prefetch: enabled->soft-preheat (reduced prefix prefetch window), quant profile: mixed->preserve-precision fallback enabled. Result: 95p latency dropped ~45% within 6 minutes on test shard. Collecting logs for next steps.

2026-03-13 08:42 - Engineering on-call (SRE): Confirmed that evict storms correlate with prefix prefetch growth. Suggested safe restore path: snapshot tenant model state (snapshot id sn-20260313-01), apply staged traffic-split, and restore snapshot to legacy optimizer profile if needed.
2026-03-14 07:58 - Ethan Kim (Support): Customer approved snapshot restore procedure for up to 20% traffic if improvements not sustained. Preparing runbook and dry-run plan.
2026-03-14 12:15 - BlueCrest SRE (Customer): Proceed with snapshot restore on approval; we'll keep escalation channel open on #support-bluecrest.

2026-03-14 12:45 - Ethan Kim (Support): Executed snapshot restore dry-run (non-traffic): created sn-20260314-dryrun, validated integrity. Next step: live partial restore gated by traffic-split script.
proposed_action_plan:
Stepwise safe rollback plan prepared by Support/On-call SRE:
1) Snapshot: create a full tenant snapshot (sn-<timestamp>) to allow atomic restore.
2) Staged traffic-split: route 5% -> legacy-profile, monitor 20m for 95p/99p latency + kv-eviction.
3) Incremental degrade script (automated): reduce async-batch.max_concurrency in steps (64->40->24->12) with 10m stabilization windows.
4) KV-prefetch soft-preheat: switch from aggressive prefetch to on-demand preheat for long-session routes.
5) Quantization fallback toggle: enable preserve-precision fallback kernel for critical decode paths.
6) If 20% staged traffic shows consistent improvement, expand split 20->50->100 with monitoring and runbook checkpoints.
7) If regressions persist, perform tenant snapshot restore to pre-change snapshot and open a postmortem to safely re-run optimization experiments with tighter preflight checks.
resolution: In progress — staged degrade scripts tested on 5% and dry-run snapshot created. Awaiting customer confirmation to progress to 20% partial restore if improvements hold. No full tenant restore performed yet.
resolution_notes: Dry-run snapshot sn-20260314-dryrun validated. 5% traffic-split reduced 95p latency by ~45% in the test shard and reduced KV-eviction rate to baseline. Customer agreed to a controlled 20% staged restore pending 60m stability window. Follow-up: schedule an ops-assisted guided restore and create a per-tenant runbook template to avoid recurrence.
follow_up_actions: Schedule ops-assisted 20% staged restore with SRE on-call (ETA 2026-03-15)
Create runbook excerpt for tenant-specific optimizer preflight checks (owner: eng-infra)
Add telemetry alert for KV-eviction rate >0.2/sec per tenant to avoid future thrash
File postmortem ticket if full snapshot restore is needed
